alcohol_template.oh: A — Broad, rounded, slightly asymmetric O–H basin, not a narrow notch or a perfectly symmetric Gaussian. Ethanol descends across approximately 3650–3400 cm-1, has a low, rounded floor at 3350–3300 with y≈12, then recovers toward 3050 before merging into C–H absorption. Propan-1-ol has a higher-wavenumber minimum near 3450, y≈6, and a long recovery toward 3100. Canonical shape: steepening entry, a short flattened/rounded bottom, and an unequal recovery shoulder. Preserve the broad envelope; do not fix every alcohol's minimum at the same position.
alcohol_template.ch: B — Compact, unequal-depth, jagged C–H multiplet superimposed on the low-wavenumber shoulder of A. Ethanol has a sharp dominant dip near 2985, followed by smaller teeth around 2945 and 2910. Propan-1-ol has a much deeper, crowded group across approximately 2980–2860, with minima around 2965, 2935, 2905 and 2875. These are partly resolved notches sharing a depressed envelope, not isolated evenly spaced spikes. Recovery toward 2800–2600 is gradual rather than an immediate return to baseline.
alcohol_template.co: C — Strong, split, irregular C–O-region cluster. Ethanol: descending shoulder from approximately 1120, a deep component near 1075, partial recovery, then the deepest component near 1035, y≈8, followed by rapid recovery by approximately 995. Propan-1-ol: a more crowded train with deep components near 1120 and 1075, a conspicuous recovery around 1045–1030, then additional deep structure around 1000 and 970. Canonicalize the split-cluster morphology, not one identical peak pattern for all alcohols; this region also contains coupled fingerprint vibrations.
alcohol_template.fpr: D — Heterogeneous fingerprint landscape: broad depressed envelopes carrying unequal local notches, interrupted by genuine recovery windows. Ethanol has a relatively smooth depression across approximately 1650–1250, a separate sharp dip near 895, and a broad, shallow low-frequency undulation. Propan-1-ol has stronger structure around 1465 and 1383, additional bands near 1240 and 1165, and a much denser 1150–900 region. Avoid either a flat fingerprint region or a uniformly dense picket fence. The terminal propanol dip near 430 is trace-specific, not a mandatory alcohol feature.

ketone_template.co: E — Very deep carbonyl notch embedded in a wider asymmetric depression. In acetone, the approach is already falling around 1850–1800 cm-1; the steep core runs through approximately 1735–1690 and bottoms near 1715 at y≈4. The bottom is narrow but rounded, not a mathematical V. Recovery through 1670–1600 reaches only a depressed local background, not immediately y≈95. Draw a broad shoulder plus a much sharper core, retaining unequal sides and finite bottom width.
ketone_template.ch: B — A comparatively shallow C–H group, not the near-saturated multiplet of the supplied propanol trace. Acetone has its clearest dip near 3005, y≈66, with weaker neighboring structure around 2965–2926, and recovers toward baseline by approximately 2800. Keep this group visibly less prominent than the carbonyl and the strongest fingerprint bands. Do not turn the shallow upper-frequency irregularities into a canonical alcohol O–H basin.
ketone_template.fpr: D — Several distinct intensity and width classes. Preserve moderate structure around 1434–1421, a strong narrow band near 1363, y≈13, and another strong narrow band near 1223, y≈12. These sit on broader depressed backgrounds and are separated by substantial recovery. Include weaker structure near 1093 and 903, followed by a relatively open 1000–700 region. The lower-frequency sag and sharp feature near 531 describe this supplied acetone trace, not universal ketone markers. A carbonyl plus two token weak fingerprint peaks would miss the observed intensity hierarchy.

acid_template.oh_canyon: F — Exceptionally broad, asymmetric, structured acid O–H canyon spanning approximately 3600–2500 cm-1. The trace descends progressively through 3400–3200, remains deeply depressed across roughly 3200–2900, and contains sharper C–H teeth near 2986 and 2948. Its low-wavenumber side has shelves and undulations around 2830–2666 before a pronounced recovery across approximately 2630–2510. Canonical shape: a wide uneven basin with embedded sharp structure and a stepped exit, not an enlarged alcohol Gaussian or an entirely flat rectangular trough.
acid_template.carbonyl: E — Deep rounded carbonyl core near 1716 cm-1, y≈4, but with a substantially broader asymmetric pedestal than in the acetone example. The high-wavenumber side is already sagging across approximately 2100–1800, reaches y≈12 at 1750, and enters a short low floor around 1728–1700. The low-wavenumber side rises through 1660–1620 and returns near baseline around 1580. Preserve the broad approach, finite floor and unequal recovery; do not transplant the acetone notch unchanged.
acid_template.co_fingerprint: G — Dense, high-contrast acid fingerprint complex, not one isolated C–O spike. Across approximately 1500–1050, strong unequal dips occur near 1485, 1460, 1430–1416, 1290, 1260–1240, 1210, 1180–1165 and 1100–1080, with incomplete and irregular recoveries. Especially emphasize the strong structured 1300–1150 region. After recovery near 1030, broader features appear around 933 and 848, followed by more separated low-frequency bands. Treat this as a mixed C–O/O–H-deformation/skeletal fingerprint region, not as an assignment of every notch to C–O stretching.

what_luna_got_right: The supplied encodings preserve the experimentally characteristic hierarchy of shapes: broad envelopes, sharper embedded minima, overlapping multiplets, asymmetric shoulders, unequal recovery levels, quiet intervals and molecule-dependent fingerprint density. They distinguish an alcohol basin from an acid canyon and distinguish acetone's narrow carbonyl core from the acid's broader carbonyl depression. This assessment concerns the supplied coordinates; fidelity to the original GIFs cannot be checked here.
what_generator_must_copy: A–G here are local morphology labels extracted from these inputs, not a claim about an independently specified IRSP taxonomy: A alcohol O–H basin; B C–H multiplet; C alcohol C–O cluster; D heterogeneous fingerprint field; E carbonyl core with pedestal; F acid O–H canyon; G acid fingerprint complex.

Use descending wavenumber, 4000 to 400 cm-1, and interpret the supplied y values as a 0–100 transmittance-like scale: absorption points downward. Preserve local backgrounds rather than resetting the curve to 100 between bands.
Generate multiscale contours: broad envelopes, medium-width depressions and narrow resolved notches. Three isolated symmetric Gaussians cannot reproduce these traces.

Use asymmetric control-point templates with shape-preserving interpolation. Retain rounded or briefly flattened minima, shoulders, partial recoveries and occasional shelves; avoid spline overshoot below zero or artificial oscillations.
Preserve relative depth, width, spacing and overlap. The strongest fingerprint bands can approach the carbonyl in depth, while C–H bands need not all be strong.
Keep real recovery windows and compound-specific complexity. Ethanol, propan-1-ol, acetone and propanoic acid should not share the same generic fingerprint texture.
Transfer morphology, not every traced wiggle or exact coordinate. Small baseline irregularities are optional texture, not automatically additional molecular vibrations.

Use SMILES to select chemically appropriate motifs and connectivity-dependent variants. Exact band positions, widths and intensities also depend on phase and measurement conditions; label the resulting exam drawing as schematic rather than an experimentally predicted spectrum.
